instrument_name: NYS DOL Minimum Wage page (rates as of 2027-01-01; 2027 off-ramp notice)
authority: New York State Department of Labor
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage NYC and Long Island & Westchester 17.00/h; remainder of state 16.00/h; unchanged on 2027-01-01 because an off-ramp condition (Labor Law 652(1-b)(d)) was met. Tipped service employees cash wage 14.15 (tip credit 2.85) NYC/LI/W, 13.30 (2.70) rest; tipped food service workers cash wage 11.35 (5.65) NYC/LI/W, 10.70 (5.30) rest; tip credit only for hospitality employers. Home care aides from 2027-01-01: 20.00 NYC/LI/W, 19.00 rest (capped at 3.00 above standard minimum). Governor proposal to change off-ramp: not enacted (proposal only).

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 652 Minimum wage (subd. 1-a, 1-b indexation and off-ramps)
figure_or_rule_carried: From 2026-01-01: 17.00 NYC; 17.00 Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester; 16.00 remainder. From 2027-01-01 adjusted annually by the commissioner: current rate x rate of change in average of three most recent Aug-Jul 12-month periods of CPI-W Northeast (NSA), rounded to nearest 0.05; no increase if (i) CPI-W change negative, (ii) NY U-3 3-month avg rises >=0.5 pt over 12-month low, or (iii) July nonfarm employment below April and below January; off-ramp limited to two consecutive years; commissioner publishes by 1 October for 1 January.

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 191 Frequency of payments
figure_or_rule_carried: Manual worker paid weekly, not later than 7 calendar days after end of week earned (semi-monthly only with commissioner authorization for employers averaging 1,000+ NY employees, or nonprofit); commission salesperson at least monthly, by last day of following month, written signed commission agreement kept 3 years; clerical and other worker at least semi-monthly on regular paydays designated in advance. 191(3): on termination, wages paid not later than the regular payday for the pay period in which termination occurred; by mail on request. Revision displayed: 2014-09-22.

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 192 Cash payment of wages (direct deposit consent)
figure_or_rule_carried: No employer may, without advance written consent of the employee, directly pay or deposit net wages in a bank or other financial institution; not applicable to bona fide executive/administrative/professional employees earning over 1,300 USD/week, nor to farm employees not connected with a factory. Pay-card rules (12 NYCRR Part 192) not read.

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 193 Deductions from wages (revision 2026-07-03; dual text with 2028-11-06 switch)
figure_or_rule_carried: Deductions only (a) required by law/regulation, (b) voluntarily authorized in writing, for the employee's benefit, after written notice of terms, limited to listed categories (insurance, pension/health, charity, US bonds, union dues, transit passes, gym, cafeteria/vending, pharmacy, tuition, day care, nonprofit-hospital housing, similar); authorization kept during employment + 6 years; (c) overpayment recovery and (d) advance repayment per commissioner regulations. Pre-tax plan deductions deemed made under law. Revocation honoured within 4 pay periods or 8 weeks. NB on the official text: this expanded version is marked effective until 2028-11-06, after which a shorter text applies. Site shows most recent revision 2026-07-03 (content of that change not isolated).

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 195 Notice and record-keeping requirements (full text incl. 195(4) retention, 195(6) termination notice)
figure_or_rule_carried: 195(3) wage statement with every payment: dates of work, employee and employer name, employer address and phone, rate(s) and basis, gross, deductions, allowances claimed as part of minimum wage, home care aide benefits, prevailing wage supplements, net; non-exempt: regular and overtime rates and hours; piece-rate counts. 195(4): payroll records kept not less than six years (hours per week, rates, gross, deductions, allowances, sick leave provided, net). 195(1) hire notice acknowledgement kept six years. 195(6): written notice of exact termination date and benefits cancellation date within 5 working days after termination. Statute silent on electronic delivery. Adds local file and 195(4)/(6) to US-NY-P5-1-003.

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 196-b Sick leave requirements (incl. 4-a paid prenatal personal leave)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with <=4 employees: up to 40 h unpaid (paid if net income > 1,000,000 USD prior tax year); 5-99 employees: up to 40 h paid; 100+: up to 56 h paid per calendar year. Accrual >= 1 h per 30 h worked from hire; may front-load. Paid at regular rate or minimum wage if greater; minimum use increment max 4 h. Carryover of unused leave required, use may be capped at 40/56 h. No payout of unused sick leave on separation. 4-a: from 2025-01-01, 20 hours paid prenatal personal leave per 52 weeks, hourly increments, regular rate, no payout. Summary of accrued/used on request within 3 business days. NYC (>=1M population) may enact greater local law.

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 198-c Benefits or wage supplements (vacation pay as wage supplement)
figure_or_rule_carried: Benefits or wage supplements (expense reimbursement, health/welfare/retirement, vacation, separation or holiday pay) owed under an agreement must be paid within 30 days after due; does not apply to exec/admin/professional earning > 1,300 USD/week. Statute fixes no automatic payout of accrued vacation on termination; payout follows the employer's written policy/agreement (forfeiture-notice rule is DOL guidance/case law, not read).

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 203-d Employee personal identifying information
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer shall not, unless required by law: publicly post or display an employee's SSN; visibly print SSN on ID badge or card incl. time card; place SSN in files with unrestricted access; communicate PII (SSN, home address/phone, personal email, internet ID/password, mother's maiden name, driver's licence number) to the public. Civil penalty up to 500 USD per knowing violation; no-policy = presumption of knowing. SSN is not a required pay-statement field under 195(3); no truncation rule for pay statements located.

instrument_name: NYS-50 Employer's Guide to Unemployment Insurance, Wage Reporting, and Withholding Tax (Revised December 2025), HTML edition
authority: NY Department of Taxation and Finance / NY Department of Labor
article_or_section: Highlights; 1 (UI); 2 (wage reporting); 3 (withholding: I, J, K, M, O, W-2); 5 (new hire); NYS-1 due dates
figure_or_rule_carried: NYS-45 quarterly combined withholding/wage/UI return due Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31 (next business day if weekend/holiday); Parts A, B, C must all be completed; e-file mandatory, balance by ACH debit; 50 USD penalty per paper document and per non-electronic payment. NYS-1: remit within 3 business days (prior-prior-year withholding >= 15,000 USD) or 5 business days after the payroll that brings accumulated quarter withholding to >= 700 USD; below 700 remit with NYS-45; new employers 5 business days. No W-2 copy is filed with NY; quarterly Part C per-employee wages and NYS/NYC/Yonkers withholding replaces it; W-2 State wages box = federal box 1 for residents and for nonresidents with any NY service (before IT-2104.1 allocation); NYC Local box = federal box 1 for full-year NYC residents, resident-period wages for part-year. New hire: report to DTF within 20 calendar days of hire date (first day of paid services) incl. rehires after 60+ days separation; electronic filers two monthly submissions 12-16 days apart; fields: employee name, address, SSN, hire date, employer name, address, EIN, dependent health insurance availability and qualifying date; nonresident alien: 20 days from SSN issue. 2026 UI wage base 17,600 USD; from 2026 = 18% of state average annual wage (4 latest QCEW quarters), rounded up to 100, never reduced. Nonresidents: withhold on NY-source wages; IT-2104.1 allocation; 14-day rule TSB-M-12(5)I. Yonkers nonresident: no withholding if Yonkers wages expected <= 3,000. Household employers: income tax withholding voluntary, wage reporting/UI if cash wages >= 500 USD in a quarter. Agricultural UI liability: >= 20,000 USD cash wages in a quarter or 10+ farm workers on a day in 20 weeks; H-2A excluded. Exempt from withholding: Tax Law 671(a)(3) under 18 / over 65 / full-time students under 25 with no prior and expected liability. UI exclusions: daytime elementary/secondary students (except nonprofit/government/tribe), ordained ministers (nonprofit), babysitters under 18 for households. Employment tax records kept at least 4 years.

instrument_name: 12 NYCRR Part 142 Minimum Wage Order for Miscellaneous Industries and Occupations (DOL official copy CR 142 (12/25))
authority: New York State Department of Labor
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x regular rate per FLSA s.7/13 methods, after 40 h/week (non-residential) or 44 h/week (residential employees); FLSA 13(a)(2),(4) exemptions not applied; FLSA-exempt employees (other than exec/admin/professional) get overtime at 1.5x basic minimum rate. Call-in pay: at least 4 h or scheduled shift if less, at basic minimum. Spread of hours > 10 h or split shift: one extra hour at basic minimum. Executive and administrative exemption salary from 2026-01-01: 1,275.00 USD/week NYC, Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester; 1,199.10 USD/week remainder of state. Meal credit 2026: 5.80 per meal NYC/downstate, 5.50 remainder; lodging credit 7.15 per day NYC/downstate, 6.75 remainder (further lodging rows 13.60 / 12.80 per day); uniform maintenance pay 2026: 21.10 high / 16.75 medium / 10.10 low weekly NYC/downstate, 19.85 / 15.80 / 9.55 remainder. Document heading: as amended effective June 24, 2020; revision label CR 142 (12/25).

instrument_name: 12 NYCRR Part 190 Minimum Wage Order for Farm Workers (DOL official copy CR 190 (12/25))
authority: New York State Department of Labor
figure_or_rule_carried: Farm worker minimum wage 2026: 17.00 NYC/Nassau/Suffolk/Westchester, 16.00 remainder. Overtime 1.5x regular rate for hours over 60 (2020), 56 (2024), 52 from 2026-01-01, 48 from 2028-01-01, 44 from 2030-01-01, 40 from 2032-01-01 per workweek. Document heading: effective February 22, 2023; label CR 190 (12/25).

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 170 Hours of labor for domestic workers
figure_or_rule_carried: Domestic worker (Labor Law 2(16)) overtime at >= 1.5x normal wage rate after 40 hours/week, or 44 hours/week for live-in domestic workers.

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 132 Employment of minors 16 or 17 (employment certificate)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minor 16-17 may be employed only on an employment certificate/permit under the Education Law (exceptions when school attendance not required: farm work, caddy, babysitting, casual yard/household chores). Minimum wage for minors = general minimum (no youth rate located in 652 or Part 142 as read).

instrument_name: NY CPLR section 5231 Income execution (creditor garnishment)
figure_or_rule_carried: Income execution: up to 10% of gross income; nothing withheld in a week unless disposable earnings exceed the greater of 30 x federal minimum hourly wage or 30 x NY Labor Law 652 minimum hourly wage in effect when payable; amount withheld not more than the lesser of 25% of disposable earnings or disposable earnings above that floor; where support deductions under 5241/5242 also apply, creditor withholding limited to 25% of disposable less support deducted; no income execution on hospital/health-professional medical-debt judgments. Disposable earnings = earnings less amounts required by law to be withheld. Two or more executions: priority rules in 5231(j). Departs from CCPA (adds 10%-of-gross cap and a state-minimum-wage floor).

instrument_name: NY CPLR section 5241 Income execution for support enforcement
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer begins deductions no later than first pay period occurring 14 days after service; remits within 7 business days of payday to the State Disbursement Unit (42 USC 654b), spousal-only support paid to creditor. Limits: 50% of disposable earnings if supporting another spouse/child (55% with arrears > 12 weeks), else 60% (65%). Support levy/5242 order takes priority over any other assignment, levy or process; multiple support executions prorated; current support > health insurance premium share > arrears add-on. Notify issuer promptly on termination (last address, new employer); levy lapses unless rehired within 90 days. Income execution notice states employer's processing fee (amount not fixed in the section read).

instrument_name: NYS DOL Form IA 12.3 Record of Employment (12/25)
authority: New York State Department of Labor
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer must complete and give IA 12.3 to each worker who is permanently, indefinitely or temporarily laid off, discharged, quits, or has hours reduced to 30 or less per week. Form carries date given, NYS employer registration number, FEIN, employer name, payroll-records address, optional payroll/clock number and work location; employee completes name and SSN. Timing deadline and statutory cite (12 NYCRR 472.8 / Labor Law art. 18) not printed on the form (not read).

instrument_name: Instructions for Form IT-201 (2025) Full-Year Resident Income Tax Return
authority: NY Department of Taxation and Finance
article_or_section: Line 21 (414(h)); Line 23 (other additions, IT-225); qualifying pension line

instrument_name: NY Labor Law section 198 Costs, remedies (revision 2025-05-16: pay-frequency damages for manual workers)
figure_or_rule_carried: Liquidated damages do not apply to violations of 191(1)(a) (manual workers paid weekly) where the employer paid on a regular payday no less often than semi-monthly: first violation limited to up to 100% of lost interest on the delayed wages (daily rate at Banking Law 14-a annual rate); liquidated damages of 100% of wages due apply where the employer has one or more prior final findings/orders for 191(1)(a) violations for employees doing the same work. Effective date taken from the Governor's signing (2025-05-09, tier-B lead); site revision date 2025-05-16.
